- Remove unneeded using directive

expected_issues.title: The HashSet is initialized with PSModuleInfo objects from `curModule.NestedModules`, but…
expected_issues.description:
The HashSet is initialized with PSModuleInfo objects from `curModule.NestedModules`, but since PSModuleInfo doesn't override Equals/GetHashCode, the HashSet uses reference equality for the Contains check. The `Get-Module` command results may contain different PSModuleInfo instances (different object references) for the same logical module, causing the Contains check to fail even when the module should be filtered out.

Consider using the existing `PSModuleInfoComparer` class or comparing by module name/path to ensure proper filtering:

```csharp
nestedModulesToFilterOut = new HashSet<PSModuleInfo>(curModule.NestedModules, PSModuleInfoComparer.Instance);
```

Or if `PSModuleInfoComparer` doesn't have a singleton instance, create a new instance:
```csharp
nestedModulesToFilterOut = new HashSet<PSModuleInfo>(curModule.NestedModules, new PSModuleInfoComparer());
```

expected_issues.title: `curModule` is derived from `context.ExecutionContext.EngineSessionState.Module`, but the…
expected_issues.description: `curModule` is derived from `context.ExecutionContext.EngineSessionState.Module`, but the comment says PSReadLine’s SessionState is often the engine session state. If this assumption is wrong for some invocation paths (e.g., different host / runspace), this could filter out unrelated nested modules. Consider tightening the condition (e.g., only apply when `curModule.Name` equals `PSReadLine` or when the module search provider indicates the originating session state) or add a targeted test to cover both PSReadLine-triggered completion and global `TabExpansion2` completion.
expected_issues.source_text: `curModule` is derived from `context.ExecutionContext.EngineSessionState.Module`, but the comment says PSReadLine’s SessionState is often the engine session state. If this assumption is wrong for some invocation paths (e.g., different host / runspace), this could filter out unrelated nested modules. Consider tightening the condition (e.g., only apply when `curModule.Name` equals `PSReadLine` or when the module search provider indicates the originating session state) or add a targeted test to cover both PSReadLine-triggered completion and global `TabExpansion2` completion.

known_false_positives.description: `nestedModulesToFilterOut.Contains(moduleInfo)` relies on `PSModuleInfo` reference equality. If the module objects coming from `psObjects` are not the same instances as those in `curModule.NestedModules`, the filter won’t work (or may behave inconsistently). Consider filtering by a stable identity (e.g., `moduleInfo.Path`, `moduleInfo.Name` + `Guid`, or `moduleInfo.ModuleBase`), or build the `HashSet` with an explicit comparer that matches how `PSModuleInfo` should be identified here.
